Air-Fryer Blooming Onion

A crisp, pull-apart onion with smoky spiced crumbs and a tangy Greek-yogurt dipping sauce.

Prep
Not listed
Cook
Not listed
Total
35 min
Difficulty
Not listed
Ingredients
11

Ingredients

  • 2 medium onions or 1 large sweet onion
  • 1 cup all-purpose flour
  • 2 tsp garlic powder
  • 2½ tsp onion powder, divided
  • 2½ tsp paprika, divided
  • 1 tsp dried oregano
  • 1 tsp salt and ½ tsp black pepper
  • 1 cup water, as needed, approximate amount
  • ¾ cup panko breadcrumbs
  • Cooking spray
  • Light dip: 170 g plain Greek yogurt, 1 tbsp light mayonnaise, 2 tbsp ketchup, 1 tbsp horseradish, 1 tsp Worcestershire sauce

Amounts are scaled from 4 original servings. Season to taste.

Instructions

  1. Trim the onion top and peel it, leaving the root end intact. With the root facing up, cut down toward the root to make 12–16 petals without cutting all the way through. Turn over and gently fan open.
  2. Soak in a bowl of ice water for 10–15 minutes so the petals open. Drain and pat very dry.
  3. Whisk flour with garlic powder, 2 tsp onion powder, 2 tsp paprika, oregano, salt and pepper. Gradually whisk in water until you have a thick, clingy batter.
  4. Coat the onion in batter, separating the petals so the batter reaches between them. Turn it upside down to drain excess, then sprinkle panko all over, including between petals.
  5. Place root-side down in the air fryer, mist generously with cooking spray, and cook at 350°F (175°C) for about 15 minutes, until deeply golden, crisp and tender. Add 3–5 minutes if needed.
  6. Stir together Greek yogurt, light mayo, ketchup, horseradish, Worcestershire, and the remaining ½ tsp each onion powder and paprika. Serve warm for sharing.

Cook times may vary when changing batch size.
